issues.what: The hero tea terrace is a bare grey walkway with two orange tables, four stools and two heaters. It has no canopy, tea counter, planters, lanterns, cushions, menu board or teapots, and nothing says 'tea house' or 'cozy'. It reads as a placeholder blockout.
issues.where: terrace.png, the whole deck; also visible from high.png and balcony.png
issues.fix: Add a pitched or fabric canopy over part of the deck, a small tea counter with a kettle and cups, potted plants along the rails, paper lanterns, and a warm practical light pool on each table. Fill the far end of the deck so it doesn't run off into empty space.

issues.what: The 'fully finished' terrace only adds a string of festoon bulbs. The deck is otherwise the same as stage 6: two tables, bare rails, empty far end, no shelter, no greenery. The bulbs don't light anything, so the tables and floor stay flat cool blue.
issues.where: terrace.png
issues.fix: Make the festoon bulbs actual light sources (warm point lights or a baked warm wash on the tables and deck). Add the canopy, counter, plants and props listed for stage 6. Without them the stage-12 terrace is not finished.

issues.what: The terrace floor is a flat, matte navy plane in heavy rain: no wetness, puddles, sheen or reflections, even though the street below is mirror-wet. The lighting is inconsistent and the deck looks unfinished.
issues.where: terrace.png, deck floor
issues.fix: Use the same wet-surface material on the deck as on the street, with low roughness, small puddles and rain ripples, and reflections of the heaters and bulbs.

issues.what: The terrace floor is still flat matte navy under rain, with no wet response.
issues.where: terrace.png, deck floor
issues.fix: Apply a wet material with puddle reflections of the string lights.

issues.what: The patio heaters have a flat, unlit, saturated orange collar band and a grey mushroom cap. They look like untextured primitives, and the near one fills the right third of the frame as a big flat orange slab.
issues.where: terrace.png, right side; also balcony.png and high.png
issues.fix: Model a proper heater head with an emissive element that casts a warm glow onto the deck. Replace the flat orange band with a metal finish, and keep the camera from framing the post so close.

issues.what: Same cheap heater primitives, plus the near-camera post fills the right edge of the frame.
issues.where: terrace.png, right edge
issues.fix: Same as the stage 6 heater fix. Move the capture camera or the heater so it doesn't block the shot.

issues.what: Near-camera geometry is clipped at the frame edges: an orange table edge at the bottom centre, and pink and yellow blocks at the bottom right.
issues.where: terrace.png, bottom centre and bottom right
issues.fix: Pull the camera back or remove the props intersecting the near plane.

issues.what: The same clipped orange table edge and pink/yellow blocks show at the frame edges.
issues.where: terrace.png, bottom centre and bottom right
issues.fix: Pull the camera back or remove the props intersecting the near plane.

issues.what: The street reflections fall apart into high-frequency zig-zag smears with rainbow banding and white star-like speckle noise. The road looks like a glitching starfield, not wet asphalt.
issues.where: high.png and balcony.png, road surface; konbini.png, foreground road
issues.fix: Lower the ripple distortion frequency and amplitude, blur and denoise the screen-space reflections, clamp the speckle highlights, and add a visible asphalt base colour with roughness variation so puddles read as patches rather than the whole road being a mirror.

issues.what: The same noisy, glitchy road reflections and starfield speckles.
issues.where: high.png and balcony.png, road; konbini.png, foreground road
issues.fix: Same as the stage 6 reflection fix.

issues.what: The crosswalk stripes read as thick 3D slabs floating above the water at odd perspective, not as paint on the road.
issues.where: street.png, right-hand foreground
issues.fix: Make the stripes coplanar decals or thin paint with the same wet shading as the road, and remove their thickness and side faces.

issues.what: The crosswalk stripes are the same floating slabs.
issues.where: street.png, right-hand foreground
issues.fix: Use flat decals.

issues.what: The puddle decals are flat dark blob shapes with hard edges that don't match the reflective road around them.
issues.where: balcony.png, road centre and bottom right; street.png, under the awning
issues.fix: Use soft-edged puddle masks that blend into the wet road shader instead of opaque dark shapes.

issues.what: The same dark blob puddle decals.
issues.where: balcony.png, road centre and bottom right
issues.fix: Use soft-edged, blended puddle masks.

issues.what: The bridge carries blank solid blue and magenta rectangles where signs or banners belong. They are obvious placeholder billboards.
issues.where: konbini.png, bridge side panels
issues.fix: Replace them with real signage: the tea house name in kana, glowing lettering, or a printed banner texture.

issues.what: The blue and magenta rectangles are still blank in the 'finished' stage.
issues.where: konbini.png, bridge side
issues.fix: Replace them with actual signage or banners.

issues.what: From the street the bridge is a featureless grey box girder. Nothing shows a tea terrace is up there apart from two tiny heater tops, so the hero location is invisible in the establishing shots.
issues.where: balcony.png, centre; street.png and konbini.png, the bridge
issues.fix: Give the bridge edge a warm silhouette: a canopy edge, hanging lanterns, plants spilling over the rail, and a warm underglow. Break up the girder with trim, bolts, grime or a light strip.

issues.what: The bridge is still a bare grey girder from below. A few string lights barely peek over it, and the terrace still doesn't announce itself.
issues.where: balcony.png, centre; street.png
issues.fix: Make the terrace dress the bridge edge (lanterns, plants hanging over the side, warm spill light) so it reads as the focal point.

issues.what: The konbini window is blown out to near-white, the 'AMA MART' sign blooms into illegibility, and the products are flat untextured coloured blocks. A far-left wall is also a washed-out white emissive plane.
issues.where: konbini.png, right half and left edge
issues.fix: Lower the window emissive and bloom threshold, keep the sign legible, add product label textures, and darken or fix the white wall at the far left.

issues.what: The same over-bright konbini window, blooming sign, flat-block products and white plane at the far left.
issues.where: konbini.png
issues.fix: Same as the stage 6 konbini fix.

issues.what: The new vertical cyan neon sign is heavily over-bloomed into a glowing smear at the top of frame. It pulls the eye away from the terrace and the shop.
issues.where: street.png, top centre; konbini.png, upper centre
issues.fix: Cut its emissive intensity and bloom, add legible lettering, and frame it so it supports the composition rather than competing with it.

issues.what: The wisteria and ivy foliage is huge chunky low-poly confetti. In high.png a purple wisteria mass and green leaf cards fill the right edge of the frame as clumsy near-camera blobs.
issues.where: high.png, right edge; balcony.png and street.png, ivy on the tea house
issues.fix: Use smaller, denser leaf clusters with alpha cards or finer geometry, keep foliage out of the near clip of the capture camera, and vary the green values.

issues.what: The building facades are flat dark-blue slabs with plain grey rectangle windows and repeated AC units. They have no texture, signage clutter or interior variation, so the street feels empty and cheap outside the shop fronts.
issues.where: high.png and balcony.png, left side buildings; terrace.png background
issues.fix: Add window interiors (curtains, lit and unlit variety), facade materials, small signs, pipes, balconies and grime.

issues.what: The left and back facades are still flat, untextured slabs with identical grey windows.
issues.where: high.png and balcony.png, left side; terrace.png background
issues.fix: Add facade detail and window variety.

issues.what: The staircase in the foreground is a near-black mass with no edge definition, so it is too dark to read.
issues.where: street.png, left third
issues.fix: Add rim light or bounce from the street, and nosing highlights or a wet sheen on the treads.

issues.what: The staircase in the foreground is still a near-black mass.
issues.where: street.png, left third
issues.fix: Add rim or bounce light and wet tread highlights.

issues.what: Chromatic aberration fringing on rain streaks and edges at the frame borders looks like a lens artefact, not an intentional style.
issues.where: all images, outer edges
issues.fix: Reduce chromatic aberration or remove it.

verdict: Both stages read as a decent rainy neon street blockout. The shop front with its awning, lanterns and vending machine is the only part that feels finished and intentional. The actual subject, the rooftop tea terrace on the bridge, is not there: in both stages it is a bare walkway with two tables, flat dry floor, primitive heaters and no shelter, plants or warm light. Stage 12 adds string lights, ivy and a neon sign, but the bulbs cast no light, the foliage is chunky, the sign over-blooms, and the bridge still carries blank placeholder rectangles. Glitchy, speckled road reflections, floating crosswalk slabs, blob puddles and a blown-out konbini window cheapen every street shot. Neither stage is a beautiful, finished, cozy place.
